content:
anya: Heads up — after the v2.7.4 runtime canary started at ~05:00 UTC we’re seeing p95/p99 regressions on the hosted API (chat.generate). p95 ~120ms -> 160ms, p99 ~260ms -> 420ms since ~07:15. Grafana: https://grafana.redwood/runtime/d/xyz
sam: copy. do we have a link to the full alert and the canary traffic %? :eyes:
ops-bot: [alert] runtime.latency.p99 threshold breached for chat.generate on region-us-west - triggered at 2026-03-17T07:18:23Z
mohit: I’m pulling traces now. first-pass: a lot of tail latency stems from a span called auth_introspect -> external-idp. suspicious.
lena: that matches what I saw in the sampling dashboard — upstream auth service latencies jumped at the same time. any recent auth changes in this rollout?
anya: runtime changelog lists auth client bumped from v1.2.0 -> v1.3.0 and a new token-introspection path enabled by default (we patched config in canary). I asked infra to confirm canary config.
kevin: can we bisect by traffic %? reduce canary to 0 and see if p99 falls. if yes, rollback. no need to full rollback yet.
sam: I temporarily routed canary -> 0% for region-us-west at 07:42. p99 dropped to ~270ms within two minutes and p95 back to ~130ms. looks correlated.
anya: great — that isolates the regression to the canary runtime + config. mohith, can you post a few trace ids showing the extra auth latency?
mohit: trace ids: trace-8a7, trace-9b2, trace-cc3. Typical slow span: auth_introspect 180-320ms, while in baseline it’s ~10-20ms. stack shows HTTP call to https://idp.prod.internal/oauth/introspect.
lena: config diff: canary has AUTH_INTROSPECTION_CACHE=false and AUTH_USE_NEW_PATH=true. stable has cache=true.
kevin: so we accidentally shipped with introspection caching disabled in canary. that would cause every request to hit IdP, explaining tail spikes.
anya: repro steps for devs — run a small load with header X-Redwood-Version: v2.7.4-canary and token header, see auth_introspect hits increase.
anya: example curl: 
```
curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer <sample>" -H "X-Redwood-Version: v2.7.4-canary" https://api.redwood.com/v1/chat.generate -d '{"input":"hi"}'
```
support-bot: logged support ticket #SUP-2026-034 referencing this thread
sam: mitigation plan I followed: 1) reduce canary to 0% (done), 2) re-enable AUTH_INTROSPECTION_CACHE in canary config and redeploy canary, 3) if latency persists, rollback runtime to v2.7.3 in canary and perform kernel-level bisect.
mohit: quick hotfix we can push: set cache TTL=60s and add circuit-breaker to idp calls. patch snippet:
```
AUTH_INTROSPECTION_CACHE=true
AUTH_INTROSPECTION_TTL=60
AUTH_IDP_TIMEOUT_MS=250
```
lena: note: some customers have short-lived tokens and caching must respect token binders — we need to validate cache correctness in QA before broad redeploy.
kevin: also added temporary per-client rate-limit rule for the hosted API to prevent cascading IdP overload: rate-limit 200r/s aggregated.
anya: after canary rollback p99 dropped ~sharp but not entirely to baseline — we still see small tail from warm-up. recommend re-deploy canary with cache=true and run 10k-sample smoke test.
sam: created a small canary with config applied and kicked it off at 08:30. monitoring shows auth_introspect count down 95%, p99 trending toward baseline at 08:36.
mohit: will follow up with flamegraphs and top spans, also opened PR to make auth cache default in runtime config and add a warning in runtime deploy check.
anya: customers impacted? support-bot, any escalations?
support-bot: two customers reported transient latency via support form. both handled, CS notified, credits offered if needed. ticket links: https://support.redwood/tickets/2026-1001
anya: postmortem action items: 1) add preflight config validation to prevent disabling introspection cache accidentally, 2) add synthetic tests that exercise auth paths during canary, 3) update rollout playbook to include immediate canary->0% step on p99 alert.
kevin: I’ll own the preflight check PR. sam will update the rollout playbook. mohith will add flamegraph artifacts to the incident.
anya: thanks all. marking this thread resolved unless anyone sees residual issues. :white_check_mark:
kevin: marking done, will follow-up in docs channel with remediation PR link.
ops-bot: [resolve] alert runtime.latency.p99 has been resolved at 2026-03-17T09:05:00Z"
